Keep that behaviour and the exported interface exactly as they are: `movies` stays `Signal<WatchItem[]>`, derived from store.items with all unwatched items (watched === false) before watched items, stable within each group.

The only remaining failures are two of your existing unit tests, both failing with "expected false to be true" immediately after a DOM interaction:
- the test about toggling watched when the checkbox is clicked (watchlist.spec.ts:49)
- the test about toggling watched when blank space on the row is clicked (watchlist.spec.ts:57)

Resolve them WITHOUT editing, weakening, or removing either test, in this order:

1) Rule out a genuine regression introduced by your change. Verify the template still passes each row's own movie id — not a loop index — to the checkbox handler and to onRowClick(event, id). Verify each interaction toggles exactly the intended movie exactly once: a click on a specific movie's checkbox must toggle only that movie (and must not additionally fire the row handler and toggle it a second time, which would be a net no-op), and a click on blank space on a row must toggle only that row's movie. Sanity-check with several unwatched movies whose ids do not coincide with their positions (e.g. ids 10, 20, 30): clicking the checkbox on the LAST rendered row must mark exactly that movie watched and leave every other movie untouched, and likewise via a blank-space click on that row. If you find any such defect, fix the component/template; both tests must then pass unmodified.

2) Only if the wiring is verifiably correct and the tests still fail because their assertions are positional — e.g. they assert that the first rendered movie or first checkbox is watched immediately after the click — then they are pinning the old insertion-order behaviour that the user's request intentionally changes: once other unwatched movies remain, the just-toggled movie now moves behind them, so "the first item is watched after clicking the first item" can no longer hold. In that case do NOT change the tests yourself: submit a test-change request for each affected test instead (your whole submission will be rejected and the request routed to me). I will approve a minimal, intent-preserving update: keep the real DOM interaction and keep asserting that the clicked movie becomes watched, but identify that movie by a stable identity (its id or title) rather than by list position.

Everything else must stay green and untouched: watchedCount, progress, announcement, remove, and all other existing tests must pass unmodified. You may add new tests freely — e.g. one asserting that after clicking the first row's checkbox, the toggled movie re-orders behind the remaining unwatched movies.
